_comment: Armies are troops sent out of a village. `support` armies stay at the destination and fight in its battles until recalled; `reinforce` armies join the battle there and go home after; `harass` armies (at least `harass.minCavalryShare` cavalry) strike for one round with a bonus, take only `harass.lossFactor` of their losses, and ride home. A reinforcement arriving from a different side than the horde (at least `pincer.minAngle` degrees apart) gets a pincer bonus on its first round: `scale` x its size / the horde's size, at most `maxBonus`. Villages send `reinforce.defaultShare` of their troops to any battle within `reinforce.defaultRange` hexes unless set otherwise. Armies live on the map: one that holds a hex, clears a camp, explores a site or supports a village stays there until moved, sent into a settlement or called home (reinforcements and harassers ride home by themselves, and a beaten army retreats home). An army carries its own grain: it leaves with `supply.hours` game hours of its upkeep from the settlement it leaves (as much as there is), eats its full upkeep from it, and its home village no longer feeds it; troops at home eat `supply.garrisonUpkeep` of theirs. Any village it reaches or stands in fills it up again, and what is left goes into the stores of the village it joins. Out of food, it marches `attrition.slowFactor` as fast; after `attrition.lossAfterHours` game hours it loses `attrition.lossShare` of each unit (rounded up) every `attrition.checkHours`, and after `attrition.lostAfterHours` it is lost altogether.
